title: Towards Exascale Simulations of Nanoelectronic Devices in the GW Approximation
problem: Quantum transport simulation of gate-all-around silicon nanowire transistors requires accurate first-principles modeling of strong electron-electron interactions in highly confined structures without empirical parameters, which demands extreme computational scale.
motivation: Technology computer-aided design for advanced semiconductor devices needs accurate quantum simulations from first principles to complement experimental development of next-generation transistors replacing FinFETs.
method: The authors implement the self-consistent GW approximation for many-body effects into the QuaTrEx ab initio quantum transport solver based on density functional theory and Non-equilibrium Green's Function formalism. Simulations scale to 10,560-atom transistors on GPU-accelerated supercomputers using parallel algorithms optimized for weak and strong scaling efficiency.
key_novelty: Integration of self-consistent GW approximation within ab initio quantum transport simulations enabling exascale nanoelectronic device modeling.
contributions: Implementation of self-consistent GW approximation in QuaTrEx quantum transport solver for accurate many-body electron-electron interaction modeling
Demonstration of exascale simulations on LUMI GPU supercomputer achieving 74% weak scaling and 60% strong scaling efficiency
Simulation of realistic transistors with up to 10,560 atoms on 1,800 GPU nodes reaching 69.3 Pflop/s performance

metrics.speedup: 74% weak scaling efficiency, 60% strong scaling efficiency

limitations: Abstract does not discuss validation against experiments, comparison with other quantum transport methods, or computational cost vs. accuracy trade-offs.
primary_theme: Exascale quantum transport simulation of nanoelectronic devices
